metadata.title: ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
metadata.source_organization: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) & Department of Health Research (DHR), MoHFW

clinical_presentation.definition: Acute coronary syndrome presentation with persistent ST segment elevation on 12-lead electrocardiogram or presumed new left bundle branch block requiring emergent reperfusion therapy.
typical_symptoms: Diffuse retrosternal pain, heaviness or constriction
Radiation to arms or neck or back
signs_and_physical_exam: Unequal or absent peripheral pulses (indicates Aortic Dissection)
Signs of respiratory pathology: pleuritis, pneumonitis, embolism, pneumothorax
unlikely_features: Long lasting (hours to days) or short lasting (less than a minute)
Restricted to areas above jaw or below epigastrium
Precipitated by movement of neck or arms or respiration
Pricking or piercing or stabbing type of pain
red_flags: Angina at rest or lasting more than 20 minutes

source.source_text_reference: CONSIDER ANGINA IF • Diffuse retrosternal pain, heaviness or constriction • Radiation to arms or neck or back • Associated with sweating ... ANGINA UNLIKELY IF: Variable location or characteristic ... Pricking or piercing or stabbing type of pain

diagnostic_criteria.name: STEMI Diagnosis Confirmation & Timing
diagnostic_criteria.description: The time point the diagnosis is confirmed with patient history & ECG ideally within 10 mins from First Medical Contact (FMC). All delays are related to FMC.
diagnostic_criteria.diagnostic_threshold: Diagnosis confirmed within <= 10 minutes from First Medical Contact

diagnostic_criteria.name: Electrocardiographic ST Elevation MI
diagnostic_criteria.description: ECG reveals persistent ST segment elevation in contiguous leads warranting immediate referral to primary angioplasty / thrombolysis capable hospital.

source.source_text_reference: ECG: If ST Elevation: Follow ST Elevation MI (STEMI) protocol. Refer to primary angioplasty/ thrombolysis capable hospital.

source.source_text_reference: Coronary angiography. Proceed for PCI, Radial route preferred, Preferably within 90 minutes

general_measures: First Medical Contact (FMC) diagnosis within 10 minutes
Continuous ECG monitoring and defibrillation standby if available
Oxygen administration if saturation is below 90%
Pain relief with IV morphine titrated in 2-4 mg increments q15m
medications_initiated: Clopidogrel 300 mg loading dose (or Ticagrelor 180 mg)
referral_actions: Assess if transfer to PCI capable hospital can be achieved in <= 120 minutes
If transfer <= 120 min: immediate transfer to PCI capable centre
If transfer > 120 min: immediate thrombolysis (preferably within 10-30 min), then transfer

source.source_text_reference: PCI INCAPABLE CENTRE: A. Transfer to PCI capable hospital if PCI can be performed within 120 min. If Transfer to PCI incapable hospital not feasible: THROMBOLYSE Within 12 hours of symptom onset

general_measures: Admit in ICU equipped with continuous ECG monitoring & defibrillation
Serial cardiac enzymes and echocardiography for mechanical complications
Post-thrombolysis 60-90 min ECG assessment of ST resolution
medications_initiated: Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC q12h (preferred) or Unfractionated Heparin infusion
Thrombolytic therapy if indicated (Tenecteplase, Reteplase, Alteplase, or Streptokinase)
Oral Beta-blockers if LVEF < 40% without shock/heart failure
referral_actions: If thrombolysis failed (<50% ST resolution): immediate transfer for rescue PCI
If thrombolysis successful: transfer for angiography/PCI within 3 to 24 hours

source.source_text_reference: POST THROMBOLYSIS: 1. ECG to be done at 60-90 min after starting thrombolysis to assess whether thrombolysis is successful (>50% ST settlement with pain relief) or not. 2. If successful, transfer patient for PCI within 3-24 hours. 3. If thrombolysis failed, transfer patient immediately for PCI capable hospital.

general_measures: Primary PCI pathway door-to-balloon target <= 90 minutes (<60 minutes in early presenters)
Tackle culprit artery only unless cardiogenic shock
medications_initiated: Dual antiplatelet therapy continued for at least 1 year
referral_actions: Accept emergency referrals from non-PCI centres
Provide rescue PCI for failed thrombolysis
Routine pharmaco-invasive angiography post-successful thrombolysis within 3-24 hours

source.section: PCI CAPABLE HOSPITAL / DURING PROCEDURE / POST PROCEDURE
source.source_text_reference: PCI CAPABLE HOSPITAL: 1. Proceed for PCI 2. Radial route preferred 3. Preferably within 90 minutes. DURING PROCEDURE: 1. Use unfractionated heparin 2. No routine thrombosuction 3. Tackle culprit artery only unless shock 4. DES to be preferred. POST PROCEDURE: 1. Continue dual antiplatelets for at least 1 year

nodes.label: Primary PCI Procedure
nodes.description: Perform Primary PCI within <= 90 minutes (<= 60 min in early presenters). Radial route preferred. Use UFH, DES preferred, tackle culprit artery only unless shock. Dual antiplatelets continued for at least 1 year.

source.section: PCI CAPABLE HOSPITAL / DURING PROCEDURE / POST PROCEDURE
source.source_text_reference: Proceed for PCI, Radial route preferred, Preferably within 90 minutes (<60 mins in early presenters). Tackle culprit artery only unless shock. DES to be preferred.

nodes.label: PCI Possible < 120 Minutes from FMC?
nodes.description: Determine whether door-to-balloon time with inter-facility transfer can be achieved within 120 minutes.

source.source_text_reference: PCI possible <120 mins? Yes -> Immediate transfer to PCI centre -> Primary PCI. No -> Immediate fibrinolysis.

nodes.label: Immediate Transfer to PCI Centre
nodes.description: Rapid ambulance transfer to Primary-PCI facility for door-to-balloon reperfusion within 120 minutes.

source.source_text_reference: A. Transfer to PCI capable hospital if PCI can be performed within 120 min. Immediate transfer to PCI centre

nodes.label: Immediate Fibrinolysis (Door-to-needle <= 30 min)
nodes.description: Verify absence of contraindications. Initiate fibrinolytic therapy (preferably fibrin-specific: Tenecteplase, Reteplase, Alteplase; or Streptokinase) within 10 minutes, ideally within 30 minutes of FMC. Administer loading Aspirin + Clopidogrel + Enoxaparin.

source.source_text_reference: THROMBOLYSE: 1. Within 12 hours of symptom onset, if no contra-indication 2. Preferably with fibrin specific agent Tenecteplase/ TPA/ Reteplase or Streptokinase ... Therapy to be started within 10 min preferably ... Preferably within 30 mins

nodes.label: Assess Fibrinolysis Success at 60-90 Minutes
nodes.description: Perform 12-lead ECG at 60-90 min. Success defined as > 50% ST settlement with clinical pain relief.

branches.condition: Successful fibrinolysis (> 50% ST settlement with pain relief)
Failed fibrinolysis (< 50% ST settlement or ongoing pain)

source.source_text_reference: POST THROMBOLYSIS: 1. ECG to be done at 60-90 min after starting thrombolysis to assess whether thrombolysis is successful (>50% ST settlement with pain relief) or not.

nodes.label: Transfer for Coronary Angiography (3 to 24 Hours)
nodes.description: Stable patient post-successful thrombolysis transferred for routine angiography and revascularization within 3-24 hours. Continue enoxaparin.

source.source_text_reference: 2. If successful, transfer patient for PCI within 3-24 hours. Preferably 3-24 hours

nodes.label: Immediate Transfer for Rescue PCI
nodes.description: Failed thrombolysis: immediate emergency transfer to PCI capable hospital for Rescue PCI (< 60 minutes).

source.source_text_reference: 3. If thrombolysis failed, transfer patient immediately for PCI capable hospital. Rescue PCI Preferably <60 mins

nodes.label: STEMI Presentation at 12 to 24 Hours
nodes.description: Transfer to PCI capable hospital immediately. If ongoing pain, administer thrombolysis and transfer immediately.

source.source_text_reference: PATIENT WITH STEMI IN 12-24 HOURS: Transfer to PCI capable hospital immediately. If ongoing pain, thrombolysis and transfer immediately

nodes.label: STEMI Presentation After 24 Hours
nodes.description: Coronary angiography with a view to PCI indicated ONLY if any of: Recurrent anginal pain not controlled by medical therapy, Cardiogenic shock, Acute LVF, Mechanical complication, Dynamic ST-T changes, or Life threatening ventricular arrhythmias.

source.source_text_reference: PATIENT WITH STEMI AFTER 24 HOURS: Angiography with a view to PCI only if any of following: Recurrent anginal pain not controlled by medical therapy, Cardiogenic shock, Acute LVF, Mechanical complication, Dynamic ST-T changes, Life threatening ventricular arrhythmias
